title: Why training fades, and how to make it stick
performance: right after their next training, the viewer schedules three short self-tests at growing gaps (about a day, a few days, a week or two) and uses recall instead of rereading

audience.assumed_prior: has attended workplace training and felt it fade; no memory science
audience.why: the brief's audience is working adults; the knowledge sheet assumes no prior terms
audience.motivation: voluntary to mildly required; wants their training time to pay off
audience.context: laptop or phone, often with sound, sometimes muted (captions needed)

strategy.name: concrete_first
strategy.rationale: each idea (the curve, the rereading trap, spacing) is easy to SEE in one person's week before it is named
strategy.signature_move: show it happen to Maya, then name the idea, then show it again on a second concrete case

misconceptions.belief: rereading my notes is a good way to keep training fresh
misconceptions.why_tempting: the page looks familiar, and familiar feels like knowing (F5)

misconceptions.belief: one long review session is as good as several short ones
misconceptions.why_tempting: the total time is the same, and cramming works for tomorrow (F7)

hook.sketch: Say Maya leaves a great Monday workshop with three new ideas. By Friday, most of it has gone quiet. Why?

arc.promise: in four minutes you will have a simple schedule for your very next training
arc.bridge_from_prior: sec1 opens from the feeling every viewer knows: clear on the day, blank a week later

sections.goal: the viewer can explain why most of a training fades in the first days
sections.carrier: a curve that drops steeply then levels off

sections.goal: the viewer can use a short self-test in place of rereading
sections.carrier: a side by side comparison of the two habits

sections.goal: the viewer can explain why spaced tests beat one long review
sections.carrier: a memory value that drains and refills, flatter after each test

sections.goal: the viewer can use a three-test schedule after their next training
sections.carrier: a journey across days on a calendar

arc.payoff: back to Maya after her next workshop: she tests herself three times at growing gaps and still has it weeks later

practice_ladder.what: Maya's schedule built step by step: tomorrow, a few days later, a week or two later
the viewer judges which of two plans keeps more after a month
the viewer applies the three tests to their own next training

recall_moments.prompt_sketch: Where on the curve does most of the forgetting happen? Early. Keep that in mind.
Same training, two plans: one long review on Friday, or three short self-tests spread over two weeks. Which keeps more after a month?
recall_moments.tempting_wrong: the long Friday review feels thorough, but it is massed rereading: familiar today, forgotten faster later

transfer_tasks: after your next training, put three short self-tests in your calendar: tomorrow, in a few days, and in a week or two

persona.voice: the mentor persona: a warm senior colleague
persona.delivery_notes: warm on Maya's story, calm and slower on the familiarity trap, brisk on the recap

gagne.objective: promise: a schedule for your next training
gagne.recall_prior: sec1 opens from the shared feeling of blanking a week later
gagne.present: sections in dependency order: curve, trap, spacing, plan
gagne.guidance: signature move: show it on Maya, name it, show it again
gagne.practice: quiz after sec3; faded plan judgement in sec4
gagne.feedback: quiz answer explains why the long review loses
gagne.assess: the viewer picks the better plan before hearing the answer
gagne.transfer: transfer task: three calendar entries after the next training

merrill.problem_centered: Maya's fading workshop is the running problem
merrill.activation: sec1 starts from the viewer's own experience of forgetting
merrill.demonstration: Maya's curve, her rereading, her tests are shown before being named
merrill.application: the quiz and the worked schedule
merrill.integration: the payoff and transfer task put it in the viewer's next training

mayer.coherence: one character, one metaphor (the curve), no side stories
mayer.signalling: one slowdown on the familiarity trap
mayer.redundancy: screen shows labels, days and the curve; narration explains
mayer.contiguity: each label appears as it is spoken
mayer.segmenting: four short sections, one idea each
mayer.pre_training: the curve is named before spacing is explained

arcs.relevance: every viewer has lost a training this way
arcs.confidence: a simple three-step plan, practised once before the payoff
arcs.satisfaction: Maya still has it weeks later; the viewer has the plan
